cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. That is below the 40 to 60% typically seen in production systems of this complexity, and it means a regression can reach production unchallenged.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are otherwise performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure: if the responsible engineer is unavailable, deployments cannot proceed and a failed release cannot be reversed. The lack of a practiced rollback process means each incident must be invented in real time under pressure, with no baseline for how long recovery will take or what steps are safe.

hinge_colon_budget.detail: 1/3 sentences (33%) use a hinge colon, exceeds 10%

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: The production database credentials are held by a single engineer with no documented access-handover process, and that engineer operates under a rolling month-to-month contract. This creates a critical dependency: if the engineer departs or becomes unavailable, the company loses immediate access to its production data with no established procedure to regain it. There is no compensating control. The absence of a credential-rotation protocol or multi-person access approval means a departure would require emergency reverse-engineering of database access, exposing the company to hours or days of downtime during the transition.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. The company has no process for handling data-subject deletion requests under applicable regulations. This creates exposure to regulatory sanctions and demonstrates a control gap that exists on paper and in practice.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no gate in continuous integration to prevent regressions from reaching production. The last 3 production incidents were caused by untested edge cases. Deployments are manual with no documented rollback procedure, which means a failure in production cannot be quickly reversed. The combination of low coverage, absent automation, and no recovery path creates material risk during any deployment.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords in the users table are stored in plaintext with no encryption, salting, or hashing applied. Customer authentication credentials are therefore readable by any engineer with database access, and a breach of the database exposes login details directly. This is a critical gap with no compensating control. We recommend implementing bcrypt or an equivalent password hashing function before this system handles any further user accounts, and auditing for any plaintext passwords already in the database.

Deployments are performed manually by engineering staff with no documented rollback procedure and no automation to reverse a failed release. The most recent rollback attempt took 3 hours to complete. This creates substantial risk of extended downtime if a deployment introduces a regression, and means the recovery path depends entirely on manual diagnosis and repair rather than a predictable restore operation. We recommend implementing automated deployment and rollback tooling, with documented procedures exercised in a staging environment before any production use.

Code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule or documented convention enforcing a single approach. This increases cognitive load during code review and makes it harder for new team members to learn the expected patterns. We recommend adopting a comment style guide and configuring a linter to enforce it as part of the continuous integration pipeline, treating style consistency as a blocking check rather than a guideline.
